spine: An interview question is only as useful as the benchmark you hold the answer against, and 'look for strategic thinking' is a label, not a benchmark. This article gives a functional lead who conducts interviews but does not do it for a living twelve questions worth asking, and attaches to each one a real answer that scores well, a real answer that scores badly, and one line naming the thing to score. Underneath them sits a single 1-5 anchored scale and the small set of habits (score in the room, score alone, write the evidence down) that keep the scale honest. At the end the reader can run a 45-minute interview from these twelve questions and defend every number they wrote.
coverage_note: Left out the 'skills, capabilities and qualifications' category as a set of its own items — none of the twelve questions is role-technical, and the paired strong/weak benchmark only works on a question every interviewer actually asks, so the IT, ML, sales and customer-success question banks are benched and role-technical questions get one short adaptation section after the items instead. Also left out Google's split of 'core competencies' and 'team collaboration' into separate question categories: those are competencies the twelve questions already test, not questions of their own. Behavioral, situational and culture/values questions are all covered, and covered as items rather than as explained categories.
